tob-10173: The Book of Hosea gathers the oracles of an eighth-century prophet who saw his own troubled marriage as a mirror of God’s relationship with Israel. His wife’s unfaithfulness becomes a symbol of Israel’s disloyalty, yet the message ends in forgiveness and restoration. It is among the shortest prophetic books and one of the most tender readings of divine love.
tob-10473: This second half of the Douay-Rheims Old Testament carries the story from the Psalms through the prophets to Malachi. Translated by the scholars of the English College at Douai and revised by Bishop Richard Challoner, it preserves the Vulgate’s wording in dignified English. For centuries it was the Bible read in Catholic homes across the English-speaking world.
tob-4273: Lewis Spence’s 1913 volume gathers the myths of Aztec, Maya, and Inca — plumed serpents, sun-lords, and the sad splendor of overthrown empires. From painted books and Spanish chronicles he rebuilds worlds the conquerors laid waste. The book stays a rich hoard of New World legend.
tob-10273: R. H. Charles’s Book of Enoch — ‘1 Enoch’ to sift it from later fakes — sets forth the seventh patriarch’s visions: the watchers’ fall, the walk through heaven and hell, the coming doom. Cited in the New Testament’s Jude, it is a root-book of Christian last-things teaching.
tob-4073: Vitruvius penned the one Roman builder’s handbook to survive — ten books on temples, waterworks, engines, and town-laying. His word guided builders from the Renaissance on. Gwilt’s Englishing made the old text speak our tongue. The book stays the bible of classic building.
tob-10573: 1 Clement — attributed to Pope Clement I — is the earliest Christian writing outside the New Testament. This letter from Rome to Corinth urges order and humility on a divided church. The text shows the first-century church in action. It remains essential for the apostolic age.
cia-0000102973: An October 1985 cable summing up the Soviet forced-labor system in a single report. By the mid-1980s the camps were smaller than under Stalin but still a vast network of prison mines, factories, and construction sites. Short cables like this one gave busy officials the essentials without the detail of a full assessment.
cia-0000106273: A June 1965 report on a coup group's decision to delay its move until after elections in Laos. Plotters timing their grab for power around the political calendar was typical of the country's coup culture. The report captures the strange normalcy of it all: in 1960s Laos, coups were scheduled like appointments.
cia-0000108073: A July 1966 report on the status of imprisoned American pilots in the Sam Neua area of Houa Phan province, Laos. Families back home waited years for word about airmen lost over the secret war's battlefields. The entry captures intelligence work at its most human: trying to learn whether captured men were still alive.
cia-0000108473: A weekly terrorism situation report dated July 2, 1980 — though the archive stamps the document itself May 1, another cataloging quirk. These weeklies tracked a rising tide of hijackings, bombings, and hostage-takings worldwide. The entry is one frame in the intelligence community's running film of global political violence.
cia-0000112273: A September 1965 report on British Guiana moving toward independence — the colony that would become Guyana. Its leftist leader, Cheddi Jagan, terrified Washington, which feared another Cuba in South America. The document captures the CIA watching a small colony's freedom through the lens of Cold War anxiety.
cia-0000109073: An intelligence report with an estimated publication date of July 1967 on the economic prospects for Communist China. Mao's China was lurching through the Cultural Revolution, and its economy was a black box. The report is another attempt to measure, from the outside, the wealth of a nation that published no trustworthy numbers.
cia-0000119173: An April 1964 report on the political situation in Brazil — written days after the military overthrew President Goulart. Washington quietly welcomed the coup, fearing a leftist Brazil. The document captures the CIA assessing a takeover America had cheered, in the hemisphere's largest country.
cia-0000126873: An August 1968 analysis of the costs to Czechoslovakia — and to the Warsaw Pact invaders — of the actions against Prague. Both sides paid: the occupied in freedom and wealth, the occupiers in money and legitimacy. The document is a balance sheet of aggression.
cia-0000126973: A June 1975 weekly review on Angola: a new cease-fire, fronts regrouping, and an open Soviet role — the truncated title hints at more. The superpowers were choosing their Angolan horses openly now. The document captures the proxy war dropping its mask.
cia-0000132573: Item 1 in the October 1960 series: Cuban foreign exchange reserves reportedly exhausted. The revolution was running out of money — the embargo biting. The document is the treasury, empty: the economy, in crisis.
cia-0000132673: A 1961 report: Panama expelling another Cuban consul. The expulsions kept coming — diplomacy by deportation. The document is the expulsion: the consul, ejected.
cia-0000134273: A 1959 report on new communist attempts to dominate Cuban labor. The party moved on the unions. The document is the takeover: the communists, organizing — the workers, claimed.
cia-0000135873: An estimated 1954 operational document — subject deleted — on death notices. The title is grim: announcements of killing, prepared in advance. The entry is the notice: the deaths, pre-written.
cia-0000136273: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN to SHERWOOD indicating that to speed tactical messages, SHERWOOD should do something — the truncated title cuts off what. The communications, accelerated. The entry is the speedup: the messages, hastened.
cia-0000136373: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN for ONTRICH with sitreps for July 6, 7, and 8. The July watch. The document is the trio: the days, reported.
cia-0000136873: A 1954 cable to the senior representative at LINCOLN on KUSODA not concurring with the team's exiting at K-somewhere — the truncated title cuts off the place. The exit, disputed. The entry is the dissent: the concurrence, withheld.
cia-0000137473: A 1961 file of comments — author deleted — on President Kennedy's visit to Venezuela. Someone's take on the trip, the name withheld. The entry is the commentary: the visit, assessed — the voice, hidden.
un-ga-res-a-69-73: General Assembly Resolution A/69/73, adopted in 2014. The seventy-third act. The entry is the record: the number, the year.
un-sc-res-273: Security Council Resolution 273, cataloged with the year 1963 — the numbering suggests 1969, a mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is questioned.
un-sc-res-673: Security Council Resolution 673, adopted in 1990 — aligned. The deliberations continued. The number and year are preserved; the decision belongs to the text.
un-sc-res-1373: Security Council Resolution 1373, adopted in September 2001 — the counter-terrorism resolution, imposing binding obligations on all states to criminalize terrorist financing, freeze assets, and deny safe haven. The legal backbone of the global war on terror. The resolution is the obligation: the financing, criminalized.
un-sc-res-1473: Security Council Resolution 1473, cataloged with the year 2002 — the numbering suggests 2003, a small inconsistency. The designation is kept; the date is questioned.
un-sc-res-1673: Security Council Resolution 1673, cataloged with the year 2004 — the numbering suggests 2006, a mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is questioned.
un-sc-res-1773: Security Council Resolution 1773, cataloged with the year 2006 — the numbering suggests 2007, a small inconsistency. The designation is kept; the date is questioned.
un-sc-res-1873: Security Council Resolution 1873, adopted in 2009 — aligned. The deliberations rolled on. The designation and year endure; the act is in the text.
cia-0000132773: A 1960 CIA file on Cuban developments, numbered 0000132773. The revolution's events, one more entry. The entry is the entry: the events, recorded.
cia-0000136773: A 1960 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000136773. The pre-invasion set. The entry is the set: the documents, pre-beach.
cia-0000139473: A 1986 CIA DCI hostage location task force report — number 0000139473. The search continued. The entry is the search: the task force, working.
un-sc-res-173: Security Council Resolution 173, adopted in 1962 — aligned. The Council's business continued. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d73: The Secretary of State to the President, October 29, 1943 — Document 73. The department briefed the White House. The memo is the briefing: the secretary, to the president.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d173: A draft message from the President to the Secretary of State — the truncated title cuts off the date — Document 173. The unsent words, preserved. The draft is the unsent: the message, in pencil.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d273: An editorial note — Cairo-Tehran 1943, Document 273. The editors' span. The note is the span: the gap, crossed.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d373: Bohlen minutes, November 30, 1943 — Document 373. The diplomat's record continued. The minutes are the continuation: Bohlen, minuting.
the-great-riots-of-new-york-1712-to-1873: Joel Tyler Headley chronicles New York's long history of mob violence — from colonial slave revolts to the terrible Draft Riots of 1863. Each uprising is told with a journalist's eye for drama and detail. A gripping, sobering tour through the city's turbulent past.
arxiv-2605-09073: Robots estimating their own motion from noisy sensors do better in continuous time with sensible motion priors. Holmes, Connor, Lilge, Guo, Dellaert and colleagues smooth the estimation with Gaussian process motion priors on factor graphs. The 2026 paper is state estimation for robots that move smoothly.
arxiv-2605-09273: A predictor is calibrated if its 70 percent predictions happen 70 percent of the time — multicalibration demands this across many groups, adaptively per instance. Zhiming Huang, Jamie Morgenstern, Aaron Roth, and colleagues make it online and instance-adaptive. The 2026 paper is fairness-flavored forecasting theory.
arxiv-2605-09373: Weighing the Milky Way's inner regions with axisymmetric Jeans models gives an answer — but a biased one. Tomoki Yamaguchi and Junichi Baba show the method systematically overestimates circular speed in the inner galaxy. The 2026 paper is a cautionary tale for galactic dynamicists.
arxiv-2605-09773: Steering a model's dark-triad features — narcissism, Machiavellianism, psychopathy — reveals separable antisocial circuits wired inside it. Cameron Berg, Roshni Lulla, and colleagues show that exploitation can emerge without any deception at all. The 2026 paper is interpretability research on the model's dark side.
arxiv-2605-10073: Patent representation learning guided by heterogeneous dependency graph attention — structure-aware embeddings for inventions. Yongmin Yoo, Qiongkai Xu, Zhangkai Wu, and Longbing Cao develop it. The 2026 paper is legal-tech NLP for the patent office. It embeds inventions with structural awareness.
plos-pone-0003373: Software builders introduced MetaSim in this 2008 genomics paper: a program that fakes DNA sequencing data for testing. As new sequencing machines flood labs with metagenomic data from environments like ocean water, researchers need known test data to check their analysis tools. MetaSim generates realistic simulated datasets so new methods can be benchmarked before touching real samples.
plos-pone-0003473: Vision scientists tested century-old laws of seeing in this 2008 paper. Levelt's propositions describe how our perception flips during binocular rivalry, when each eye sees a different image. The team confirmed the laws hold broadly and showed binocular and perceptual rivalry share computational machinery, pointing to common circuits behind conscious visual experience.
plos-pone-0003573: Ecologists showed hungry mouths above reshape life below in this 2008 paper. Grazing animals change how plant biomass is distributed, and the team found those aboveground bites shift the biomass and flow of soil invertebrates. The food web's upper story quietly engineers the hidden economy beneath the surface.
plos-pone-0003673: In 2008, Lucas, Guédon, and Jay-Allemand modeled how plant roots branch. Their model runs on auxin transport, the flow of the plant growth hormone through root tissues, to decide where side roots sprout. The math captures how roots explore patchy soil, a key trick for plants hunting water and nutrients.
plos-pone-0003773: Skerritt and Campbell rewired a potassium channel's gate in this 2008 paper. Swapping in a non-native R1 residue in the S4 voltage-sensing domain uniquely changed how the Kv4.3 channel opens and closes. The single swap shows how precisely evolution tuned these electrical gates.
plos-pone-0003873: Back in 2008, a group found the front end explaining two kinases' differences. The N-terminal domain of ERK1 accounted for its functional split from ERK2, despite their similarity. The domain-level answer shows how small structural differences create distinct signaling roles.
plos-pone-0003973: In 2008, Coutant, Frenkiel, and Despres tested a safer lentivirus-based vaccine. Their nonintegrative vectors delivered vaccine cargo without stitching into the host's own DNA. The vaccinated animals mounted strong and lasting antiviral immune defenses against the target. The approach keeps lentiviral vectors' punch while dodging the risk of DNA integration.
plos-pone-0004073: In 2008, Di Stefano, Calabro, and Di Gangi probed a virus in the placenta. Human herpesvirus 8 infected placental tissue in lab dishes and in the body. Placental infection can harm pregnancy and fetal growth. The work flags a new route of pregnancy risk.
plos-pone-0004173: In 2009, Mabilleau and Sabokbar split bone-cell birth from bone-cell work. Interleukin-32 drove osteoclast differentiation but not activation. The cytokine built the cells without switching them on. The split refines targets for bone-loss drugs. The distinction matters for treating osteoporosis.
plos-pone-0004273: In 2009, a team found a tumor gene guiding young fish embryos well. The tumor blocker PRDM5 tuned Wnt signals early in zebrafish growth. The regulator shaped the embryo's very first steps. The fish work clarifies early human growth too today.
plos-pone-0358873: Medical trials must report their methods by the CONSORT checklist — and sloppy reporting hides real flaws. This study asked several large language models to judge whether published trials meet CONSORT standards, then compared their verdicts. The wide variation between models warns that AI review of medical papers is not yet reliable.
plos-pone-0357773: Air pollution’s reach may extend all the way to male fertility. This rat study showed nasal exposure to PM2.5 induces testicular injury and activates pyroptosis — inflammatory cell death — signaling. The inhibitor interventions it tested point to how the damage pathway might one day be blocked.
plos-pone-0347073: Cutting emissions changes ozone and PM2.5 in fiendishly complex ways. This paper built a LASSO-based reduced-form CMAQ model predicting those responses to emission changes in South Korea. The fast surrogate model lets policymakers test clean-air scenarios in minutes instead of waiting days for supercomputer runs.
plos-pone-0357973: Rhizobium bacteria fix nitrogen for plants — but their family tree is badly tangled. This GenBank mining study revealed that identical 16S rRNA sequences are largely uncoupled from species designation, host plant, and geography. The finding shakes up how microbiologists name and classify these agriculturally vital bacteria.
plos-pone-0354073: Building dynamic models of machinery in simulation software is slow, expert labor. This research developed a dynamic model construction method based on secondary development of RecurDyn. The method automates and accelerates mechanical simulation setup, cutting the time engineers spend building models by hand.
plos-pone-0356173: Crowds aren’t uniform masses — small groups of friends and families move as units within the flow. This paper modeled the probabilistic dynamics of small groups in crowd flows. The mathematics captures how these clusters bend and shape the crowd’s overall movement, improving predictions for safety planning.
plos-pone-0357573: Diabetic nerve pain stubbornly resists most treatments. The PAINLESS trial protocol — a randomized crossover design — will test pain alleviation using hybrid closed loop insulin pumps in diabetic neuropathy. The planned trial asks a provocative question: can tighter automated glucose control actually ease nerve pain?
plos-pone-0357673: Facial prostheses weather brutally in tropical climates — cracking, fading, and failing patients. This in vitro study tested how TiO2 and SiO2 nanofillers affect the mechanical performance of maxillofacial silicone elastomer after two years of outdoor tropical weathering. The nanofillers meaningfully extend prosthesis life.
plos-pone-0357473: Biofortified cowpea could fight hidden hunger across Mozambique. This paper bioeconomically optimized zinc and iron agronomic biofortification in cowpea under real tropical field conditions. The optimization shows farmers how to grow more nutritious beans without sacrificing yield or profit.
plos-pone-0355473: The EIF1 factor coordinates gene networks that go awry in diabetic eye disease. This paper linked EIF1 to transcriptomic and splicing networks associated with cell cycle dysregulation in diabetic retinopathy. The factor emerges as a therapeutic lead for a leading cause of blindness.
plos-pone-0357273: Infant common marmosets are increasingly vital research models — yet their basic anatomy was poorly mapped. This paper histologically characterized the major internal organs of infant marmosets. The baseline atlas gives primate researchers the reference they’ve been missing.
plos-pone-0356773: Retinopathy of prematurity — eye disease in premature babies — may signal broader developmental vulnerability. This nationwide Korean Health Screening study examined ROP as a clinical marker of developmental risk in preschool children. The link turns an eye finding into an early warning system for the whole child.
plos-pone-0352873: Watching human movement conveys emotion even with no faces, no context, no labels. This paper studied affective meaning extracted from unlabeled biological motion and its associations with social–perceptual sensitivity. The findings parse how we read feelings from pure movement.
plos-pone-0357173: Forecasting hepatitis C’s trajectory is essential for elimination campaigns. This data-driven approach combined machine learning with classical epidemiological models for hepatitis C forecasting. The hybrid forecasts help health officials target interventions where they’ll matter most.
plos-pone-0356873: Dialysis patients with stubborn hyperphosphatemia need tenapanor — some at surprisingly high doses. This pooled analysis of three trials identified patient characteristics associated with needing high doses. The findings help nephrologists personalize dosing instead of guessing.
plos-pone-0355673: The social vulnerability index was built to predict disaster impacts — can it also predict gun violence? This paper assessed the index’s utility as a predictor of firearm violence, probing whether ‘misappropriating vulnerability’ works. The findings test the limits of repurposing a disaster metric for a violence epidemic.
plos-pone-0356473: Mudstone — the rock beneath countless structures — weakens as water infiltrates its microscopic pores. This molecular dynamics simulation studied its macroscopic mechanical deterioration and microscopic hydration mechanism. The atomic-scale insights help engineers predict when mudstone foundations will fail.
plos-pone-0356373: Liver biopsy via endoscopic ultrasound is delicate work — and needle technique matters. This tertiary center reported its experience with 22G fine-needle biopsy using the slow pull technique. The real-world results guide gastroenterologists toward liver sampling that’s both safer and more diagnostic.
plos-pone-0356073: Why do people trust some AI chatbots and not others? This paper examined relational intelligence in AI chatbots through a trust–engagement–emotion–social presence model, analyzed with PLS-SEM and fsQCA. The findings reveal the relational ingredients that make conversational AI feel genuinely present rather than mechanically hollow.
plos-pone-0355973: Anopheles stephensi — an invasive malaria mosquito — has reached the Horn of Africa. This paper documented its biological forms in Djibouti City. The entomological survey provides the baseline data vector control programs need to confront this urban malaria threat.
plos-pone-0355373: In Lubumbashi, traditional birth attendants use plants to stimulate labor — knowledge at risk of vanishing. This paper documented ethnomedicinal knowledge of uterotonic plants used in alternative medicine in Haut-Katanga, DR Congo. The recorded pharmacopoeia preserves both cultural heritage and leads for future obstetric drugs.
plos-pone-0355873: Ayurveda and Siddha herbo-mineral formulations are widely used against cancer — but the evidence base is murky. This paper published a scoping review protocol for their preclinical evaluation. The planned review will systematically map what laboratory science actually says about these traditional formulations.
plos-pone-0354973: Professional soccer players burn energy at rates that generic formulas misjudge. This cross-sectional study estimated resting metabolic rate in pros, comparing traditional predictive equations against a preliminary machine learning approach. The findings help sports nutritionists fuel elite athletes with precision rather than guesswork.
plos-pone-0355173: Patients awaiting spine surgery face barriers to staying active — and facilitators that help. This qualitative study explored both. The patients’ perspectives reveal what keeps pre-surgical spines moving — critical because fitter patients recover better.
europmc-pmc2791173: Neuroscientists wrote this 2009 paper to explain how bursts of chemical inhibition shape the firing of thalamus neurons during the brain's alpha rhythm, the slow electrical waves tied to vision and attention. It describes how inhibition frames when these relay cells fire, controlling the messages they pass to the cortex. The work links the alpha rhythm directly to how the brain handles what we see.
europmc-pmc2825373: Dynamic causal modeling is a powerful but tricky way to study brain connectivity from scans. This 2010 paper offers ten simple rules for doing it well. The authors, leaders in the method, distill practical wisdom for avoiding common traps. The guide helped a generation of neuroscientists use the technique correctly.
europmc-pmc2831073: Plants hit by stress can pass toughness to their young. This 2010 paper shows this handoff in Arabidopsis needs DNA marks and Dicer-like proteins. The team proves the gear behind inherited stress memory. The find showed how plants prime the next generation with no gene changes.
europmc-pmc2836773: Web pages vow to nudge habits, but do they work? This 2010 pool of trials tests online drives for health habit shifts. The authors find drives built on theory, using tried tricks, win most. Their math handed web health builders a proven recipe, not hunches.
europmc-pmc2857873: Pancreatic cancer resists surgery alone, so doctors try chemo first. This 2010 review pools trials of pre-surgery therapy in pancreatic cancer, measuring tumor shrinkage and how many patients reach the operating table. The authors' math favors the early-treatment path. The review backed a shift in how this brutal cancer is handled.
europmc-pmc2887173: Trauma surgeons now steer clotting with bedside tests. This 2010 paper studies goal-directed clotting management in major trauma using ROTEM-guided fibrinogen and prothrombin dosing. The authors show tailored dosing beats fixed recipes. Their approach cut blood use and saved lives.
europmc-pmc2955973: Prison release is a deadly window for drug users. This 2010 meta-analysis finds soaring drug-related deaths soon after release from prison. The authors' pooling demands action. Their work pushed overdose prevention at release. Tolerance drops inside, then kills outside. Naloxone at the gate saves lives.
europmc-pmc3028573: A heart failure blood marker predicts outcomes. This 2011 paper tests galectin-3 levels in two kinds of heart failure. The authors validate the marker's warning power. Their work aids heart doctors. High levels flag scarring in the heart. Doctors now order it alongside standard tests.
europmc-pmc3031573: Jumping genes tangle genome annotation. This 2011 paper urges mappers to respect jumping-gene variety when labeling new genomes. The authors' guidance sharpens genome maps. Their work aids annotators. Corn's genome is mostly jumping genes. Ignoring them garbles the gene count.
europmc-pmc3072373: Plant growth rewrites protein spools. This 2011 paper tracks a key histone mark as mustard plants build new tissues. The authors watch the mark shift with each cell fate. Their work lights up plant gene control. The mark silences genes past their prime.
europmc-pmc3072973: Heart cells got a universal recipe. This 2011 paper gives a foolproof recipe for turning stem cells into heart cells. The authors' method erased line-to-line quirks. Their work powered drug testing. Drug firms screen heart toxicity with it. The recipe is free for all labs.
europmc-pmc6518373: Drawing on 716,152 births recorded across France in 2012, this study measured what gestational diabetes costs newborns. Mothers with the condition faced higher rates of complications - oversized babies, difficult deliveries, and newborn health problems. The sheer scale of the data gives doctors firm numbers for counseling patients and shows why screening and managing blood sugar in pregnancy matters.
europmc-pmc6523673: Exosomes are nano-sized bubbles that cells release to trade proteins, RNA, and lipids with neighbors - a postal service between cells. This review covers how scientists isolate and characterize them, what they do in health and disease, and how they might be harnessed as drug-delivery vehicles or disease markers. The field is racing from basic biology toward clinical tools.
europmc-pmc6532273: Aging brains accumulate damage, and much of it traces back to mitochondria - the cell's energy factories leaking destructive oxidants. This review takes the mitochondrial view of neurodegeneration, showing how faltering power plants drive oxidative stress in Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, and ALS. Protecting mitochondria, the authors argue, may be the most direct way to protect the aging brain.
europmc-pmc6538573: Pupil size betrays mental effort, arousal, and emotion - but raw eye-tracking data is noisy. This paper gives researchers a practical cleanup manual: step-by-step guidelines plus ready-to-run code for preprocessing pupil measurements. Standardizing the boring but crucial cleaning step makes pupillometry results more trustworthy across psychology and neuroscience labs.
europmc-pmc6550273: Health apps and gadgets multiply, but patients, doctors, and insurers still do not trust them much. This paper maps a path to validation: what counts as proof that a digital health tool works, who should judge, and how standards could grow. Without credible validation, the authors argue, digital health stays a gadget aisle rather than medicine.
europmc-pmc6669473: Mold toxins in animal feed poison livestock and sneak into meat, milk, and eggs. This ten-year global survey tracked mycotoxin contamination in feed across continents. The data show where the threat runs hottest - and why monitoring feed is a food-safety must.
europmc-pmc6689873: Drugs morph inside the body - liver enzymes rewrite their chemistry. BioTransformer predicts those rewrites: a computational tool forecasting how small molecules get metabolized, in humans and in the environment. The open software helps toxicologists and drug designers see a compound's fate before it exists.
europmc-pmc6707173: Drinking during pregnancy can scar a child's brain for life - yet counting the victims has proved tricky. This 2001 summary reviews methods for estimating fetal alcohol syndrome's prevalence since the late 1970s. The takeaway: the true toll is larger than clinic counts suggest, and better counting guides prevention.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-73: This 2007 GAO report presses the nuclear weapons labs to prove their safety push is real. The labs that build and tend the nation's bombs had launched fix-up drives for both bomb work and staff safety — but GAO found no hard proof the drives worked. The report demands facts, not pledges, from the most dangerous workshops in the land.
gao-gaoreports-b-299873: General Dynamics cried foul over a 2007 tech award, and GAO's ruling is the final whistle. The defense-tech giant said the agency's pick was wrong; the call tests the protest against bid law. When industry titans clash over federal IT fortunes, this is the scorecard — public, reasoned, and binding.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-273: Open-ended Pentagon deals were bleeding in 2007 — GAO's report says time-and-materials contracts needed better insight and controls. The findings target the blank-check corner of defense buying. The report's fix: watch the clock, cap the meter, and stop paying by the shrug.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-373: Bad nursing homes needed better targeting in 2007 — GAO's report says federal helpers should aim aid where the care was worst. The findings demand smarter triage of the quality-improvement money. The report's cause: the frailest patients deserve the sharpest oversight.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-573: Food stamp sign-ups were stuck in the paper age in 2007 — GAO's report says easier application methods could use a real boost. The findings press for modernization of the process. The report's logic is humane: hunger should not require a fax machine.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-673: Tax season 2007 was a stress test for the IRS — GAO's report gives the interim filing-season results and grades the 2008 budget ask. The findings link performance to funding in detail. The report's question: did the agency earn the dollars it wanted?
openalex-w7206174973: Nurses in a hospital heart unit, where doctors thread thin tubes into patients' vessels, are expected to follow a set care process. This reflective article looks at how that process works in real life: what the evidence shows, what has improved, where the weak spots are, and what still needs work. It suggests ways to make steady, standard nursing care hold up in a fast, high-tech ward.
openalex-w7204938173: Why do some children struggle to learn to read or do math? This study looks to neuroscience for answers, examining how brain development in childhood relates to learning disorders and what that means for teaching. The authors review research on the mechanisms behind these difficulties and their classroom consequences. It bridges brain science and pedagogy, arguing that understanding the developing brain helps teachers reach struggling students.
openalex-w7202285173: Medical school grinds students down, but some bend without breaking. This study measured resilience among MBBS undergraduates and what correlated with it. The authors linked toughness to well-being. A medical-education study of the inner resources behind the white coat.
pmc-13453073: In this 2026 chemistry paper, scientists synthesized beta-thiolated amino acids as building blocks toward the total chemical synthesis of microcin J25, a lasso-shaped peptide antibiotic made by bacteria. Building such knotted molecules from scratch is a formidable puzzle. Each new fragment brings a fully synthetic version closer.
pmc-13430673: This 2026 study evaluated the quality of online abortion information available in Australia for people facing unintended pregnancy. The assessment measured accuracy, completeness, and bias across websites. For a decision this consequential, the information landscape matters — and the paper grades it.
pmc-13643773: This 2026 forestry software paper presents OptOrch, a modular optimization toolkit for deploying forest tree seed orchards — the plantations that produce seeds for reforestation. Where to plant which families decides the genetic quality of future forests. The toolkit brings rigorous optimization to the task.
pmc-13499173: In this 2026 health economics paper, researchers evaluated the cost-effectiveness of screening pregnant people for iron deficiency across different ferritin thresholds. Where to set the cutoff changes costs and benefits. The analysis guides prenatal screening policy.
pmc-13589873: In this 2026 paper, SF1 was shown to regulate FDX1 transcription to promote cuproptosis — copper-driven cell death — in pediatric sepsis-related acute lung injury, via interaction with cJUN. The newly described death pathway operates in critically ill children. The mechanism is a therapeutic lead.
pmc-13501973: A 2026 case report and literature review on concurrent resection and orthognathic surgery for mandibular condyle osteoma — a jaw joint tumor. Combining tumor removal with jaw realignment is ambitious. The case details the approach.
pmc-13466373: In this 2026 orthopedic paper, return to sport after curettage for benign and locally aggressive bone tumors was studied. Athletes want to know when they can play again. The data answer it.
pmc-13437273: A 2026 review framing ferroptosis — iron-driven cell death — as a novel mechanism and therapeutic target of traditional Chinese medicine for fatty liver disease. Ancient remedies meet modern cell death biology. The review bridges the paradigms.
pmc-13421373: A 2026 informatics paper on a standards-based, cloud-hosted clinical decision support system for gonorrhea treatment and HIV screening. The cloud CDS brings guidelines to the point of care. The standards-based design enables interoperability.
pmc-13582973: A 2026 data paper introducing MindTS-MMD — a Chinese multimodal dataset for emotion expression analysis in children with Tourette syndrome. The multimodal data capture tics and feelings. The dataset enables affective computing research.
pmc-13490873: A 2026 multicenter prospective randomized split-face study of intelligent microfocused ultrasound for lifting facial laxity. The device firm's claims were tested rigorously. The study is the evidence.
pmc-13448273: A 2026 conference abstract (RMTC-04) on risk factors associated with early brain metastases in breast cancer — a retrospective cohort study from a specialized cancer center (the record's location is truncated).
